title: Inline media in a supplier rate catalog exceeds the aggregate RPC payload budget
fault_primitive: MongoDB rate-plan import containing inline base64 image content, propagated to non-expiring Memcached entries
incident_class: Supplier feed schema mapping regression with persistent cache amplification
symptoms: Hotel searches return HTTP 500 while pods remain Running and Ready. Search logs report ResourceExhausted from rate. Individual cached rate entries fit the item limit, but a normal five-hotel gRPC result exceeds the default 4 MiB receive limit. Large rate payloads also increase serialization work.
why_hard: The visible incident resembles insufficient rate capacity or aggressive search retries, but increasing capacity cannot make an oversized gRPC message valid. The imported documents are valid BSON, indexes and credentials are intact, and prices and dates look normal. Cache entries have no expiration: repairing MongoDB alone leaves stale oversized entries, while clearing or restarting Memcached alone repopulates them from MongoDB. Application restarts and deployment rollback do not undo persistent catalog state.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Tune rate QPS, queue depth, search deadlines, or retry count without checking catalog document sizes
Scale or restart rate after seeing CPU pressure and downstream timeouts
Roll back the visible CPU and runtime tuning while leaving the imported data in MongoDB
Clear the shared cache without removing the inline media records in MongoDB
Repair MongoDB without invalidating already populated non-expiring cache entries
Increase the gRPC receive limit and retain excessive serialization and cache churn
mitigation_summary: Remove imported inventory rows whose room descriptions contain inline base64 images, drain old rate workers, then invalidate the shared rate cache. Recovery restores original rate runtime settings, search retry count, and cache arguments from existing last-applied configuration.
